preamble: Reduction of [o] to [ə] is a common outcome of stress-driven vowel reduction: in unstressed syllables the vowel loses its rounding and backness and centralizes. Russian reduces unstressed /o/ to [ə] outside the immediately pretonic syllable. Historically, Middle High German weakened the full unstressed vowels of Old High German to e [ə], so final -o in weak nouns such as namo 'name' and ohso 'ox' became name /ˈnamə/ and ohse /ˈoxs̠ə/.

languageExamples.language: Middle High German (from Old High German)

examples.note: Unstressed vowels of Old High German were weakened to e in Middle High German (OHG taga > MHG tage 'days').

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Vowel reduction in Russian. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vowel_reduction_in_Russian

context: In unstressed syllables; reduction is conditioned by stress placement
allophones_note: In Russian: unstressed /o/ outside the pretonic syllable is realized [ə]; the Middle High German entry is a historical change, not allophony
